item.title: Self-Hosted DHCPv6 Servers: Kea vs odhcpd vs Dnsmasq
item.description: As IPv6 adoption grows across home networks, enterprise infrastructure, and cloud environments, the need for reliable DHCPv6 servers has become essential. While many self-hosted networking guides focus on IPv4 DHCP, running a dedicated DHCPv6 server requires different considerations — from stateless vs stateful address assignment to prefix delegation for downstream routers.

item.title: Self-Hosted NAT64/DNS64 Gateway: Jool vs TAYGA vs Ecdysis
item.description: NAT64 and DNS64 are complementary protocols that enable IPv6-only clients to communicate with IPv4-only servers — a critical capability as networks transition to IPv6. NAT64 translates IPv6 packets to IPv4 at the network layer, while DNS64 synthesizes AAAA records from A records when no native IPv6 address exists. Together, they allow organizations to deploy IPv6-only internal networks while maintaining full access to the IPv4 internet.

item.title: Self-Hosted IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Tools: ndppd vs CoreRAD vs NDP Library (2026)
item.description: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (ND) replaces ARP, ICMP Router Discovery, and redirect protocols from IPv4 with a unified ICMPv6-based protocol suite. It handles address resolution, duplicate address detection, router advertisement, and neighbor unreachability detection. However, many network environments need to extend or modify ND behavior – proxying ND across subnets, controlling router advertisements, or implementing custom ND security policies.
